note_tweet.text:
"Hard Times Create Strong Men" – Where the Meme Really Comes From

Everyone has seen it: hard times create strong men, strong men create good times, good times create weak men, and weak men create hard times. The wording comes from a 2016 survival novel. The idea is six centuries older, and it was written by a man most of the West has never heard of.

1. The man. Ibn Khaldun was born in Tunis in 1332. He was a historian, a judge, a diplomat, a courtier and a prisoner, and he served and survived half the courts of North Africa and Spain. In 1401, when Tamerlane besieged Damascus, the old historian had himself lowered down the city walls on ropes to go and meet the conqueror. The man who studied conquerors went to interview the greatest one alive.

2. The bond. His key word is asabiyyah, the bond: the feeling of a group whose members would die for each other. Desert tribes have it because they must. They have no walls and no police, only each other. City people lose it because they no longer need it. So strength is not muscle. Strength is the bond.
This is Civilization: people bound to one another, building something that outlives them.

3. The four generations. A dynasty lasts about four generations. The builder knows what it cost. His son knew the builder and keeps the standards. The grandson imitates without understanding, following rules whose reasons he never saw. The great-grandson thinks greatness is his birthright and despises the effort that built it – and then he destroys it.

4. Everyone knows it. The Germans say: acquire, inherit, ruin. The English say: shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in three generations. The Chinese say wealth does not survive three generations. You have seen it in a family business too: the founder’s grandson with the Porsche and the "vision".

5. The tax curve. Ibn Khaldun also noticed that at the start of a dynasty taxes are low and revenue is high, while at the end taxes are high and revenue is low, because people stop bothering to work. That is the Laffer curve, six hundred years early. Reagan quoted him on it in 1981.

6. The West. The generation of 1945 rebuilt Europe from rubble. Their children kept the standards. Their grandchildren imitate the forms – elections, institutions, speeches – without the bond. And now an heir generation is taught to despise the inheritance. Ibn Khaldun even described the next step: the declining dynasty hires others to defend it. Europe outsourced its defense decades ago.

7. The correction. The meme is wrong in one place. Hard times do not create strong men. They create strong bonds, and the bond makes the men strong. Good times do not weaken men only through comfort. They weaken them by making the bond unnecessary – family replaced by the state, the tribe replaced by the screen.

Hard times will come anyway. They will not make us strong. They will only find out whether we are still a Civilization – or just a population.
